system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every point. Several departures matter beyond the headline numbers:

- **Hidden overrides.** Two clauses would quietly push all claims through the general regime, including title, fraud and specific indemnities. These are the "all Claims" limitation clause and clause 9.3/12.8/20.5.
- **Disclosure combined with buyer knowledge.** General data-room and register disclosure, plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar, would together empty out most of the warranty protection.
- **Admissions against the Seller's own position.** The Disclosure Letter concedes that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, the Ironquay assignment and the bonus funding are all **unresolved**. The cover note frames them as "addressed", "agreed" or "adequate".
- **Stale disclosure.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Any facts we rely on need to be refreshed against the current DD record.

None of the Seller's labels ("key negotiated positions", "agreed price mechanics", "considered adequate", "settled", "fair and balanced") reflects agreement on our side. We should treat each as an opening position.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1)
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Issue:** The figure exactly matches our conditional fallback. That does not make it acceptable. The fallback can be used **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft, and none has been given. A matching number is not clearance. The cap's real value also depends on what sits underneath it: thresholds, carve-outs, disclosure and knowledge. Here all of those are adverse, so 20% on these terms is worth much less than 20% on our terms.
- **Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal the fallback. If the deal team wants to use it, seek Amelia Frost's written authority referencing this draft first. Present it only as part of a package that restores our positions on thresholds, carve-outs, disclosure and knowledge.

### 1.2 Thresholds: AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, excess only (cl 12.2)
- **Playbook:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; once exceeded, the Seller is liable from the first dollar.
- **Issue:** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The basket also works as a deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined with the higher de minimis, mid-sized claims (for example AUD 20,000 items) would never count towards the basket. The first AUD 250,000 of loss would sit with us permanently.
- **Push back:** Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket. Confirm that claims below the de minimis still count towards the basket for related or recurring matters. Thresholds must not apply to fundamental claims, specific indemnities, tax or fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits: 18 months, plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, and none has been given.
- **Issue:**
  - 18 months is again our fallback offered as if it were the starting point. The same logic as the cap applies.
  - The second sentence is the more dangerous one. It is a hidden general-regime override that flips the default: every limitation applies to every claim unless we remember to carve it out each time. This conflicts with our requirement to keep the Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate.
- **Push back:** Restore 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence. Each regime should stand alone, and general limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims expressly.

### 1.4 Fundamental and title warranties under general caps and time limits
- **Playbook:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at 20%. If title fails, we may not own what we paid AUD 24m for, yet recovery would be limited to AUD 4.8m within 18 months, after a AUD 250,000 deductible.
- **Push back:** Reject outright. Capacity, authority and title sit in a standalone fundamental regime on playbook terms.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This position is not waivable by anyone.
- **Issue:** "Of any nature" catches fraud, specific indemnities, the fundamental warranties and covenant or payment claims. A non-reliance clause that covers fraud is especially objectionable.
- **Push back:** This is a red line. Insert an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out that overrides clauses 9.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5 and the caps and thresholds. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses so they do not apply to the fundamental, tax, specific indemnity, covenant or payment regimes.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure of the whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Issue:** Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or *referred to*" in the data room. That could reach documents we never saw. Clause 1.2 adds publicly searchable records with no limit. Together they would qualify almost every warranty.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Only the specific disclosures in sections 2 to 10 should qualify warranties, and only to the extent they are fair: fact and scope identified with enough detail for a buyer to assess them. The data room can be identified for reference, but not deemed disclosed. Disclosures must not qualify the fundamental warranties, and must not cut back specific indemnities, which exist precisely because we know about those matters.
- **Also:** Clause 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable as non-admission. Ensure it cannot be read as limiting the warranties or indemnities themselves.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge bar: any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was discoverable (cl 8.3)
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** This is about as broad as such a bar gets. It covers advisers' knowledge and matters merely "discoverable", which in practice brings in constructive knowledge. Because we have diligenced Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005 and DD-006, it would arguably extinguish claims on exactly the issues we have identified, including any specific indemnities we negotiate.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If the Seller insists, offer at most an actual-knowledge qualifier limited to named deal-team individuals and to specific fair disclosure. It must not reach advisers or "discoverable" matters, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. Separately, insist that Seller-side knowledge qualifiers in the warranties are tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Facts:** DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The change-control consent is in cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. Disclosure Letter section 2 confirms the Seller has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Issue:** The cover note says this is "addressed". The Seller's own disclosure shows it is not. Two parts of the proposed mechanism are unacceptable:
  - Reasonable endeavours is too weak for a customer worth about 30% of revenue.
  - "Satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" means a consent that is conditional, qualified or not yet effective would still satisfy the condition. That leaves the cl 11.3 conditions unaddressed.
- **Push back:**
  - Make effective Bluefen consent a condition precedent. The consent must be unconditional, or its conditions fully satisfied.
  - The Seller must deliver evidence, before Completion, that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied.
  - Raise the obligation above reasonable endeavours (for example all reasonable or best endeavours) and require the Buyer's approval of the consent's form.
  - The CP should be waivable only by the Buyer.
  - Ask for an updated status, since the letter is dated 22 September.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Facts:** DD-003 shows about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. Disclosure Letter section 3 confirms it has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Issue:** A release "to be provided following Completion" would leave Riverlark security over the target, and a possible change-control default, while we are the owner. That is inconsistent with a debt-free / cash-free deal. "Approximately" AUD 3.2m is also not a current payout figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter from Riverlark.
  - Repayment should be made directly to Riverlark from Completion funds and deducted from the price.
  - All security releases, PPSR discharges and returned documents should be delivered at Completion.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so this is not currently on the table.

### 3.3 DD-005 completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 excluded from the funds flow
- **Facts:** Disclosure Letter section 5 confirms the bonuses do not appear in the funds flow and does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Issue:** "A matter for the Seller" without itemisation is exactly the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. The bonuses are triggered by Completion, and the target is the employer. In practice the liability, and any on-costs, would land on the Company and therefore on us.
- **Push back:**
  - Either itemise AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding, any workers' compensation) as a specific deduction or Debt-like line item in the funds flow, or require Seller funding at Completion paid through payroll.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket.
  - Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position and the continued-employment conditions.
  - Do not let the "agreed price mechanics" wording pass. The mechanics are not agreed.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP indemnity: limited to the SOW3 payment (cl 11.1)
- **Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but that is not bank-verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Issue:** An indemnity limited to the payment leaves the actual risk with us: that the IP has not passed, or that Ironquay asserts rights in the materials. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. We should not treat it as owed, or as paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of title to or right to use the Ironquay or SOW3 materials, any Ironquay claim, and the cost of cure.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: the Seller procures payment of whatever is verified as outstanding, and delivers evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment, ideally before Completion.
  - Keep this indemnity outside the general regime.
  - Ask for bank evidence and an Ironquay statement of account.

### 3.5 DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, exact scope and any notification duty are all unknown. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Issue:** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an unsupported conclusion. The Seller's own disclosure says these questions are not yet established. We should equally not overstate it: on current information there is **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or loss figure, and we should not put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete the materiality characterisation.
  - Add pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs and evidence, to complete the investigation (with external forensic support if appropriate), and to give the Buyer regular updates and access to findings.
  - The Buyer should be consulted before any notification decision under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme, but the Company must remain free to comply with law.
  - Add a specific indemnity, uncapped by the general regime and with no numeric amount, for losses arising from the incident.
  - Do not let general disclosure or buyer knowledge qualify this.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals: AUD 330,000
- **Facts:** DD-008 and DD-011 show three related renewals at AUD 110,000 each. The Seller's disclosure itself declines to say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Issue:** The cover note asserts "ordinary-course operating costs" without support. The playbook also cautions us not to assume the opposite, so we should not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from the price.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. Ask for the contracts, timing, termination rights, accrual treatment and the business rationale, including why there are three linked renewals. Then decide on the treatment, which may be ordinary course, a working-capital adjustment, a Debt-like item or a warranty or covenant point. Pending that, add a conduct-of-business covenant restricting further renewals without Buyer consent.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties: "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** These terms remain open. Assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution.
- **Push back:** Reject the "settled" framing. Tax and IP stay in their own categories, and their terms are to be negotiated. Do not concede that they sit under the general cap, basket or time limit. Equally, do not represent that we have secured unlimited liability.

### 3.8 Title: evidenced by the share register at DD-012
- **Playbook:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority is required. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Issue:** Disclosure Letter section 10 itself concedes that it only "identifies the source relied on" and does not suggest verification.
- **Push back:**
  - Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract and historical searches, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, share issue and transfer history with stamped transfers and board minutes, and evidence of the Seller's corporate authority and capacity.
  - At Completion, require original share certificates, executed transfers and any releases of share security.
  - Full title warranties in the fundamental regime, unqualified by disclosure or knowledge.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller characterises the lease as notification-only and the Mossvale restriction as not triggered by a share sale. These are reasonable on their face but are the Seller's characterisations. They should be **verified by our own review** of the provisions, including any change-of-control definitions, rather than accepted. Add the lease notification as a Completion deliverable or covenant. If our review finds that either clause is triggered, add consent as a CP.

---

## 4. Process points
- **Refresh the source facts.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Request a bring-down: updated status on the Bluefen consent, the Riverlark payout, the Ironquay payment, the DD-006 investigation and the Sandbar renewals. Distinguish verified updates (documents and third-party evidence) from Seller assertions.
- **Internal authority.** No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) is authorised. If the team wants flexibility, the request goes to Amelia Frost in writing, identifying this draft.
- **Disclosure Letter drafting.** Insist that it does not qualify the fundamental warranties or specific indemnities, and that specific disclosures are given against the specific warranties they qualify.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Hold 25% / AUD 6m.** No fallback authority exists, and a matching number is not clearance. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping (first dollar).** |
| 3 | General time limit | 18 months | **24 months.** No fallback authority. |
| 4 | "Limitations apply to all Claims" | Default override | **Delete.** Keep regimes separate. |
| 5 | Fundamental / title | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.** |
| 6 | Fraud and misconduct | Caught by limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance | **Red line: full carve-out from everything.** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Delete 1.1–1.2. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, includes advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete.** At most named persons with actual knowledge; never for title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met before Completion.** Stronger endeavours obligation. |
| 10 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | **Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion.** |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Itemise AUD 420k plus on-costs, or Seller-funded, with an indemnity.** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-payment indemnity | **Broaden to IP title and claims, preserve the SOW3 cure.** AUD 180k unverified; get evidence. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Delete characterisation. Preservation, investigation, update covenants, plus a specific indemnity.** No assumed breach or quantum. |
| 14 | Sandbar AUD 330k | "Ordinary course" | **Investigate before classifying.** No automatic Debt treatment. Covenant on further renewals. |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Open. Separate categories.** No assumption of unlimited liability. |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC, PPSR, transfer and authority evidence.** Full title warranties. |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | **Verify independently.** Add a lease notification deliverable. |
| 18 | Stale disclosure | As at 22 Sept 2026 | **Require a bring-down and refreshed evidence.** |

**Priorities for the mark-up:** Items 6, 5, 4, 7 and 8 are structural and non-negotiable. Items 9, 10 and 11 are Completion-mechanics essentials with real money at stake. Items 1 to 3 should be held at playbook positions, with no fallback used unless Amelia Frost gives written authority for this draft.
=== END ADVICE ===
